label: Autonomous customer support agent
blurb: Third-party LLM agent with write access to production ticketing and email. The scenario the case study is written around.

input.business_owner: D. Okafor, Director of Customer Operations
input.business_purpose: Resolve tier-1 customer support tickets end to end without analyst involvement, including issuing account credits under a fixed threshold.
input.description: An LLM-based agent that reads inbound support tickets and the customer's account record, searches the internal knowledge base and past ticket history, drafts and sends the customer reply, updates the ticket status and fields in the production ticketing system, and issues account credits up to $200 by calling the billing API. It runs continuously against the inbound queue and escalates to a human only when it cannot classify the ticket. Ticket content and knowledge base articles are placed directly into the model context. The team has invested in platform hygiene - workload credentials are held in a secrets manager, egress is allowlisted, and agent activity is logged - but the agent holds the same broad application role as a human support analyst and no action it takes is reviewed before it reaches the customer.
input.model_provider: OpenAI GPT-4o via vendor SaaS platform

label: Internal policy assistant (read-only)
blurb: Retrieval assistant over internal policy documents. No tools, no write access, human in the loop.

input.business_owner: M. Reyes, Head of Internal Comms
input.business_purpose: Answer employee questions about internal HR and IT policy by retrieving and summarising approved policy documents.
input.description: A retrieval-augmented assistant over the internal policy library. Employees ask a question in a chat interface; the system retrieves the relevant approved policy sections and returns a summarised answer with citations to the source document. It has no ability to take action, send messages, or modify any record. All answers display the source passage alongside the summary so the employee can verify it.

label: Semi-autonomous infrastructure agent
blurb: Internal agent with cloud infrastructure permissions including delete. Approval required only for actions it classifies as high impact.

input.business_purpose: Automatically remediate low-severity cloud misconfiguration findings and clean up orphaned infrastructure resources.
input.description: An internally built agent that consumes cloud security posture findings, decides on a remediation, and applies it via infrastructure APIs. It can modify security group rules, rotate credentials, and delete orphaned resources such as unattached volumes and idle load balancers. It classifies each action's impact itself and requests engineer approval only for actions it judges high impact. It runs on a schedule against the findings backlog.

label: Adversarial test case (worst plausible)
blurb: A deliberately dangerous configuration used to prove the engine responds to compounding risk. Every agent risk modifier is at or near its ceiling.

input.business_purpose: Automate the full customer lifecycle: onboarding, account changes, billing adjustments, retention outreach and offboarding, without analyst involvement.
input.description: An agent with standing write access to the production customer database, the billing platform and the outbound email system. It reads customer records including payment details and support history, decides on account actions itself, calls partner APIs to provision and deprovision services, and emails customers directly. It has no approval gate on any action, runs continuously, and shares an application role with the operations team. Credentials are held in the deployment configuration. Outbound network access is unrestricted so the agent can reach any partner API without a change request. No logging of tool calls or agent reasoning is in place, and no monitoring exists beyond uptime checks.
input.model_provider: Third-party agent platform, model not disclosed
